findings.title: The public evaluator preselects controls before validating stateful child transitions
findings.summary: The exported evaluator builds a control chain from statically parsed carriers before it derives the accepted parent epoch state. The complete child-control validator exists but is not part of the authoritative public path.

findings.title: A selected child control carries only base heads rather than their exact accepted ancestor closure
findings.summary: The evaluator resets accepted history to the child frontier identities. A frontier is not the full state. Ancestors can be incorrectly excluded or omitted from materialization.

findings.title: Actor counters and causal epoch rules are not enforced by the public change-acceptance path
findings.summary: The repository contains actor-state and epoch helpers, but the public evaluator reduces semantic validity primarily to device membership, write role, and terminal state. Sequence, start_op, empty-change frontier, exact predecessor, base ancestry, and exact-closure application are not composed into acceptance.

findings.title: Normative interoperability still runs through a parallel simplified evaluator
findings.summary: The interop runner accepts abstract control/change vectors with caller-supplied valid flags and independently reimplements chain selection, dependency acceptance, heads, and digests instead of using signed carriers and ReferenceEvaluator.

findings.title: Canonical dispositions and report semantics are incomplete and internally inconsistent
findings.summary: The public digest includes only change hashes, invalid changes are folded into excluded_changes, dynamic control invalidity is not reported, and Completion::Failed extends the canonical vocabulary without a matching NIP/report-schema contract.

findings.title: The requirement matrix is structurally fail-closed but not evidence-semantic
findings.summary: The generator assigns broad path-based proofs and defaults unclassified requirements to out-of-core. The validator proves row shape and path existence, not that an exact test or fixture executed and passed for the reviewed commit.

findings.title: Carrier validators reject unknown tags that the NIP requires clients to ignore
findings.summary: Change, control, manifest, descriptor, and chunk validation impose exact total tag sets or non-normative forbidden tags. The NIP requires exact required-tag cardinality, explicit expiration/protected-tag rejection, and otherwise ignored unknown tags.

findings.title: Unsupported-revision preclassification bypasses strict canonical JSON validation
findings.summary: Carrier classification uses ordinary serde_json parsing to inspect v and format before duplicate-member and canonical-JSON enforcement. Ambiguous or duplicated declarations can be classified as unsupported rather than invalid.

findings.title: Work accounting, cancellation, and panic resistance are incomplete across the full public path
findings.summary: Graph scheduling improved, but control scans, transition validation, checkpoint preparation, state projection, and some grouping work remain unmetered or recursive. Evidence-derived paths still use unreachable! assertions.

findings.title: Materialized projection loses mark expansion and can conflate nested conflicting object branches
findings.summary: The projector preserves many scalar and text details, but mark expansion is absent. Descendants of conflicting objects can share an indistinguishable ordinary path, and the conformance runner selects the first path match.

findings.title: Empty-history checkpoints are rejected by implementation-only head and change-count rules
findings.summary: The NIP requires a nonempty serialized snapshot and valid chunks, but does not require at least one change or head. The implementation rejects change_count zero and empty heads.

findings.title: Checkpoint refusal families are catalogued but not all executed through signed public-engine fixtures
findings.summary: Positive signed checkpoint integration exists, but the report test checks inventory and recorded gate labels. The complete negative matrix is not driven through exact signed descriptor/chunk/control/change evidence.

findings.title: The checked-in interop attestation does not bind the reported final Rust and private TypeScript commits
findings.summary: The combined report binds earlier implementation commits and a six-fixture simplified corpus. The final closure report names later commits without a matching final signed-corpus manifest and canonical output digest.

findings.title: Production and publication assurance remains incomplete
findings.summary: Sustained native Rust fuzz execution and independent security/protocol review remain explicitly unperformed. Resource evidence does not qualify every provisional maximum or supported mobile/relay environment.
